prior_finding_resolution.HOT_HANDLE_TTL: The three independent original failure scenarios now pass on this exact candidate: expired hot retry, expired write guard, and a real recovery response arriving after expiry.

reproduction: Use actual UI and loopback HTTP to save original BEGIN with a private reason, or VERIFY_P1 with a private reason and sources.
Issue the next legitimate REPORT_FAILURE_P1 or BEGIN_P2 and intentionally lose its actual saved HTTP response.
Advance only browser Date.now beyond the original handle expiry, then use hot recovery.
The expiry guard correctly rejects without any new GET/POST, discards pending and handle and preserves a read-only view.
The read-only view was made by spreading the old full view; its raw event remains, including the previous private reason. The VERIFY scenario also retains the full event.sources snapshot.
findings.impact: The invalid-handle fallback violates the frozen minimum projection and privacy contract. This is retained private data in servicePlanView, not an observed new unauthorized read, external disclosure, repeated submission or database write.
findings.minimal_fix: Construct the invalidated minimum projection using explicit safe fields, including event:null and minimal step/event/history fields. Preserve drafts and existing history references, but do not retain previous raw body/source objects. Add real page tests after a previously successful BEGIN/VERIFY.

checks: Original three TTL failures independently rerun and passed.
Delayed original ADOPT after NOT_OBSERVED can commit; the page still never replays it.
Cold unknown plus current EXECUTE revocation denies recovery and delayed original submission.
Second generation ADOPT recovery stays bound to its previous generation after third adoption.
Explicit invalid key headers are rejected without business state changes.
Hot retry/release rejects missing or changed localStorage and retains a valid same-name replacement.
Stored handle mutation while an actual GET is in flight refuses the old 200; a current actual 403 takes priority and clears private views.
Previous successful original BEGIN and VERIFY raw event privacy both fail.

code_review.new_change_scope: The backend recovery, original CAS and event proof logic are unchanged from d5. The new product changes are confined to browser validation and fallback projection; no new business command/table/migration/grant.
code_review.expiry_and_storage: Hot GET, response acceptance, original POST response acceptance and release reread the strict stored handle and compare all eleven fields. Same-name valid changed metadata is preserved. Invalid state does not automatically POST or call the ordinary observation-writing plan GET.
code_review.auth_context_priority: Current 403 remains prior to storage invalidation; stale context is rejected by the original generation/preparation/token fence before responses are accepted. Independent current-403 plus stored-key-change test passed.
code_review.readonly_backend: Backend recovery still calls _view with event=None, observe=False and fresh_clock=True and then minimizes events/history and sources. No matching raw event field is introduced in the server recovery response. Independently rerun business snapshots and authority/deadline cases are in the related regression.
code_review.fallback_privacy: The invalid-handle client projection is incomplete because object spread retains raw event. This blocks the candidate despite the fixed original TTL scenarios.

remaining_limits: Do not merge this candidate into dev until repaired, normally pushed and independently re-reviewed.
